official.deadline_central_display: 16 April 2027 (closing date of the announced 2027 application window for Japanese nationals)
official.deadline_note: Conflicting official dates: the World Bank's live Japanese Nationals page announces the 2027 window running from February 15 to April 16, 2027, while the 2027 Application Guidelines PDF states the portal deadline as April 21st, 2027 at 12:00 noon EST. April 16, 2027 and the 2026 closing date of Friday April 17, 2026 both fall on a Friday, which supports the live page's date, and the Guidelines PDF also carries stale 2026 text elsewhere ('winners informed by June 2026'). Plan against 16 April 2027 and re-check the official page when the window opens.
official.application_cycle: 2027 cycle; application window for Japanese nationals announced as February 15 to April 16, 2027
official.status_note: The World Bank has announced dates for the 2027 application window for Japanese nationals, which opens February 15, 2027. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, and the Japanese-nationals application portal link on the World Bank page is not live yet.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For the duration of the scholarship period, tuition for his/her graduate program and the cost of basic medical insurance that can be obtained through the university.
official.funding_period: one-off per trip, paid twice (start and end)
benefits: The scholarship is fully funded by the Government of Japan.

One economy class air travel from the scholar's home country to the host university at the start of the graduate degree program (if the scholar is not already attending the graduate program), plus a $600 travel allowance.

One economy class air travel from the host university to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment at the end of the scholarship period, plus a $600 travel allowance, conditional on the scholar having completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree.
For the duration of the scholarship period, tuition for the graduate program and the cost of basic medical insurance that can be obtained through the university.

While on campus during the scholarship period, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses (accommodations, food, etc., including books); the amount of the allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published.
eligibility: On or after the date the call for scholarship applications opens, not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment (including temporary and consultant) of the World Bank Group, and not be a close relative of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew).
Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) earned at least three years before the date of the Application Deadline.

On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as staff or any type of appointment, including temporary and consultant) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank.

Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline.

At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries.

Online graduate degrees, and graduate degrees related to Foreign Service, Diplomacy, Business (including MBAs) and Law (including LLMs), Medicine (including MDs), or any joint programs with a Japanese university are not eligible for financing by the JJ/WBGSP scholarship.
requirements: Submit only one complete application electronically through the JJ/WBGSP application portal by the application deadline; applications delivered in person, by fax, email or postal mail are disqualified, and individuals who submit more than one application are disqualified.

Do not submit the application until an unconditional (except for financing) letter of acceptance from a PhD or master's program in a development-related field at a university located outside Japan has been uploaded.

Two professional recommendation letters, submitted online, from people who have direct knowledge of the applicant's professional work experience; one is not sufficient and three or more is not permitted.
One academic recommendation letter, submitted online, from a professor the applicant has collaborated with on a research project or paper.
One completed Application Form (including the applicant's agreement to the conditions stated on the signature page) written in English or the language of the PhD or master's program.

The JJ/WBGSP scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if notified as a semi-finalist or awarded, the applicant must inform and document other sources of scholarship funds to the Secretariat. The stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if the Program has evidence of undeclared external funding.
documents: Scanned documentation that proves the applicant meets the eligibility requirement regarding the number of years of recent development-related work.
The applicant's bachelor's degree diploma, and if applicable the diploma of the most advanced graduate degree (a transcript may not be substituted for a diploma).

C.V. using the format provided in Annex 2 of the Application Guidelines, written in English or the language of the master's degree program for which JJ/WBGSP funding is sought; unpaid work must be listed under a 'Volunteer Work' category and not as employment.

Unconditional (except for financing) Letter of Admission for the upcoming academic year to a master or doctorate program for which the applicant is seeking JJ/WBGSP funding, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence.
Translations of any documents not in English or the language of the degree program; both the original and the translated document must be uploaded, and a certified translation is not required.

For finalists: a scanned copy of the identification page of the passport (or birth/marriage certificate) with the name identical to the application form, within three business days of the scholarship offer; and a medical doctor's certificate less than three months old, submitted at least 21 days before traveling to the host university.
selection_criteria: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10, taking into account four main factors and the degree of cohesion among them.
Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight).
Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight).

The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors, the requirement of unconditional admission (except for financing and/or medical certificate), maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender, and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad; finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee (World Bank Board of Directors members and WB management) for approval.
coverage: Tuition for the graduate program for the duration of the scholarship period.
Cost of basic medical insurance that can be obtained through the university.
A monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus (accommodations, food, etc., including books); the amount varies depending on the host country.

One economy class air travel from the home country to the host university at the start of the program plus a $600 travel allowance, and one economy class air travel from the host university to Japan or a developing country with secured employment at the end plus a $600 travel allowance.

Not covered: visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses that do not meet the minimum credits required to earn the graduate degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, expenses related to research, supplementary educational materials, field trips, participation in workshops/seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee.
application_method: From February 15, 2027, express interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org.
Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or be currently enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD program outside Japan.

Complete the Recommendation Request Form early in the process, identifying the two professional recommenders and one academic recommender, then submit the online Application Form through the JJ/WBGSP application portal (accessible only on a computer, not a cell phone).

Submit one complete application, including scanned diplomas, Annex 2 CV, proof of development-related work and the unconditional admission letter, before the announced window closes on April 16, 2027 (the Application Guidelines PDF states April 21st, 2027 at 12:00 noon EST).

Await the decision; winners are informed by mid-July after JJ/WBG Steering Committee approval, and successful finalists must supply the passport identification page within three business days and a medical certificate at least 21 days before travel.
official.application_route: One online application through the JJ/WBGSP application portal linked from the World Bank Japanese Nationals page; email, postal or in-person applications are disqualified.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be Japanese nationals; the funded graduate program must be located outside Japan and outside the applicant's country of citizenship and residence.
official.international_eligibility: Only Japanese nationals are eligible for this track; the funded study must take place outside Japan. (The separate developing-country-nationals track of the JJ/WBGSP covers other nationalities.)
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The program must be in an area of study related to development. Online graduate degrees, and degrees related to Foreign Service, Diplomacy, Business (including MBAs) and Law (including LLMs), Medicine (including MDs), or any joint programs with a Japanese university are not eligible for financing. World Bank Group staff and close relatives, and Government of Japan/JICA/local government/Central Bank employees from the opening of the call, are excluded.
official.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less.
official.description: The JJ/WBGSP provides scholarships for up to two years to a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals who are dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries, and who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD graduate degree program outside of Japan and in development-related fields. The scholarship is fully funded by the Government of Japan.
official.region: Asia (Japan); the funded study must take place outside Japan
official.program_type: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP), Japanese nationals track, fully funded by the Government of Japan and run by the World Bank
official.english_requirement: No IELTS/TOEFL or MOI score is published. The Application Form and the Annex 2 CV must be written in English or in the language of the master's or PhD program being applied for, and any document not in one of those languages must be uploaded together with an uncertified translation. Recommendation letters must be written in English, or in French or Spanish where the target master's or PhD program is taught in that language.

not_confirmed: monthly subsistence allowance amount (the FAQ states the value of the scholarship is not provided to applicants and depends on the length and location of the program, and that the monthly allowance varies by host country; only the US$600 per-trip travel allowance is published)
the exact binding closing date of the 2027 window (the live page announces April 16, 2027 while the Application Guidelines PDF states April 21, 2027 at 12:00 noon EST)
English test scores (no IELTS/TOEFL or MOI requirement is published; only a language rule for the application documents and recommendation letters is published)
verification.notes: World Bank Japanese Nationals page, the official 2027 Application Guidelines for Japanese Nationals and the official 2027 FAQ for Japanese Nationals (both PDFs on thedocs.worldbank.org, updated August 2026) were all checked. The $600 per-trip travel allowance, benefits, exclusions, selection weights, eligibility, documents, language rule and the unpublished subsistence allowance come from those pages. The 2026 window is confirmed closed (17 April 2026) and the 2027 window announced but not yet open, so the programme page date is used as the central deadline with the guidelines' later date flagged.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the World Bank's JJ/WBGSP, funded entirely by the Government of Japan, and it pays a complete package rather than a flat stipend: tuition, university-arranged basic medical insurance, a monthly living allowance set by host country, two economy-class flights and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The only cash figure the World Bank publishes is that US$600, so you cannot budget the award's total value from any official source. The 2027 window runs 15 February to 16 April 2027, and you cannot submit anything until an unconditional (except financing) admission letter is in hand, so your university applications have to come first. Expect the award to act as a supplement: any other funding you hold must be declared and can reduce or void the stipend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Japanese mid-career professionals with at least 3 years of paid development-related work earned in the past six years who already hold, or are about to hold, an unconditional (financing excepted) offer for a development-related master's or PhD outside Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Email scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org on or right after February 15, 2027 so the Secretariat registers your interest before you invest weeks in the portal
Secure an unconditional (except for financing and/or medical certificate) letter of admission for the upcoming academic year; a waitlist, conditional or one-year-deferred offer does not qualify

Count your 3 years of paid development-related work backwards from the Application Deadline and within the past six years, then collect employer evidence; the self-employed need the government registration document for the organisation

Line up exactly two professional referees who observed paid development work and one academic referee from a research collaboration, and confirm their institutional email addresses before sending the Recommendation Request Form
Build the CV strictly on the Annex 2 template with month/year dates, exclude unpaid internships and volunteer work from employment and list them separately
Work on a desktop or laptop, never a phone, and submit at least a week before the deadline as the Secretariat recommends
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the application before the unconditional acceptance letter has been uploaded, or relying on a waitlist or conditional offer
Recommenders missing the deadline; an application without all three recommendations on time is considered incomplete and is not reviewed at all
Studying an excluded field (MBA, LLM, MD, Foreign Service, Diplomacy, fully online, or a joint programme with a Japanese university)
Counting unpaid internships, volunteer work or a period of graduate study toward the 3-year paid development-related employment requirement
Submitting more than one application, or attempting to apply by email, fax, post or in person
Holding other funding without declaring it; the stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially where undeclared external funding is found
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa application and resident permit fees, any cost of bringing or supporting family, a computer, language training outside the programme, additional travel during the study period, research costs, supplementary materials, field trips, workshops/seminars and internships, the enrolment deposit your university may ask for to hold your place, plus any gap between the host-country subsistence allowance and local rents.
document_audit: Diplomas must be uploaded as diplomas; the FAQ is explicit that a transcript cannot be substituted, and several diplomas for the same degree should be scanned into one file
Do not upload transcripts or GPA documents as extra evidence: the FAQ states additional academic documentation is not wanted
Documents not in English or the programme language need both original and translation uploaded, but certified translation is not required and free translation tools are acceptable
If your documents carry different names, for example after marriage, explain the variation in the last question of the Statement of Purpose
Self-employed or founder applicants must upload the government registration document; an unregistered organisation counts as volunteer work, not employment
The signature field must be typed, not an uploaded image of a signature
alerts: The programme page window (February 15 to April 16, 2027) and the guidelines' portal deadline (April 21, 2027, 12:00 noon EST) differ; both closing dates fall differently against the historical Friday pattern, so submit comfortably before the earlier date
The 2026 window closed on 17 April 2026 and the Japanese-nationals portal link is not live yet, so nothing can be submitted today

Notification timing is stated inconsistently across the official documents: mid-July on the programme page, 'by June 2027' in the Guidelines and 'likely by June 1st, 2027' in the FAQ, so do not plan your leave around a single date
The World Bank deliberately does not publish the scholarship's cash value or the monthly subsistence amount, so plan your budget from your host city's own cost of living
If you are accepted unconditionally by more than one programme you must choose one before applying, and the award cannot be transferred later
It is your responsibility to judge your own eligibility; the Secretariat will not assess your circumstances or make exceptions
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the Secretariat from February 15, 2027 to register interest, build one application on a desktop through the JJ/WBGSP online portal, have your three recommenders submit through their own emailed unique links, upload the admission letter and diplomas, then wait for two-assessor scoring, Secretariat shortlisting and Steering Committee approval, with winners informed around mid-year.

official.deadline_note: No exact dates are published. Recruitment runs in two periods per fiscal year through the host departments: Period I around February for students whose studies at Kyushu University begin between April and September, and Period II around May for students whose studies begin between October and March. Because applications are made through the prospective host department, that department sets its own internal deadline within the round; the FY2018 edition of the scheme guidelines still on Kyushu's site set the department-to-university deadlines at 2 February and 31 May respectively.
official.application_cycle: Recurring scheme with two recruitment periods per fiscal year (Period I around February for April-September starts; Period II around May for October-March starts); no dated 2026/2027 call is published
official.status_note: A standing, recurring scheme with two recruitment periods per fiscal year rather than a dated call. As of the published rules, the next recruitment after an October standpoint is Period I around February, for stays beginning April to September.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of 80,000 yen (支給額 月額80,000円), published on Kyushu University's INVITATION site for prospective international students.

Kyushu University's own support program for privately financed international students, available to Special Auditing Students, Special Research Students, and Double Degree Program Students who have few opportunities to apply for scholarships.
Open even to international students from universities without a student exchange agreement with Kyushu University (as special auditing or special research students).

Cap: if the applicant receives other scholarships, the monthly amount of the scholarship (or the monthly equivalent of the total if scholarships are received from multiple organizations) will not exceed 80,000 yen.

Kyushu University's faculty-level descriptions of the scheme state that examination, matriculation and tuition fees are waived according to the relevant exchange agreement; the central pages publish no such waiver.
eligibility: Those who do not have Japanese nationality.

Applicants must be a student at an overseas university, and the host status in the department or school of Kyushu University must be one of: international students under inter-university exchange agreements (special auditing students, special research students); international students under inter-departmental exchange agreements (special auditing students, special research students); international students under double degree agreements (double degree program students); or international students from universities without student exchange agreements (special auditing students, special research students).
Acceptance in Japan must begin within the academic year, and the period of stay must be either 3 months, 5 months (1 semester) or 11 months (2 semesters).
Those who are unable to study in Japan solely at their own expense due to financial reasons.
Those who are certain to obtain 'Student' status of residence when studying at Kyushu University.

After completing their studies at Kyushu University, students must return to their home university to continue their studies and obtain a degree or graduate (those scheduled to withdraw or be expelled, and those who graduate or complete a regular course of study during their studies at Kyushu University are not eligible).

Applicants must have excellent academic records and character, and a grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher (on a 3-point scale) for the previous year at the time of selection at the applicant's home institution (evaluation coefficient based on a calculation method specified by the Japan Student Services Organization).

If the applicant receives other scholarships, the monthly amount of the scholarship (or the monthly equivalent of the total amount if the applicant receives scholarships from multiple organizations) will not exceed 80,000 yen.
requirements: If you wish to receive this scholarship, contact and apply for it through your prospective host department at Kyushu University.
Acceptance in Japan must begin within the academic year, for a stay of 3 months, 5 months (1 semester) or 11 months (2 semesters).
After completing studies at Kyushu University, the grantee must return to the home university to continue studies and obtain a degree or graduate.
The combined monthly amount of this and any other scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed 80,000 yen.
A grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher on a 3-point scale for the previous year, based on the calculation method specified by the Japan Student Services Organization.
The grantee must be certain to obtain 'Student' status of residence while studying at Kyushu University.
selection_criteria: Under the Kyushu University Friendship Scholarships Scheme, Kyushu University invites students from abroad who attend prestigious universities in their home country and who will play an important role in their nation's future, aiming to foster the nation's future leaders, maintain good relations with Kyushu University, and act as a point of contact to cultivate joint research.
Selection is carried out through the host department at Kyushu University.

The published main requirements applied in receiving the scholarship: non-Japanese nationality, qualifying host status (special auditing, special research or double degree student), a stay of 3, 5 or 11 months beginning within the academic year, inability to study in Japan solely at own expense, certainty of obtaining Student status of residence, commitment to return to the home university, and a grade evaluation coefficient of 2.30 or higher on a 3-point scale (JASSO calculation method).
coverage: A monthly scholarship of 80,000 yen for privately financed international students on special auditing, special research or double degree status.
Ceiling: the total monthly amount of this and any other scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed 80,000 yen.
Paid monthly for the period of stay, which must be 3 months, 5 months (1 semester) or 11 months (2 semesters) and must begin within the academic year.

The FY2018 edition of the scheme guidelines on Kyushu's own domain states the scholarship is paid from the university-cooperation fund and is conditional on being enrolled at Kyushu University for at least 16 days of the month, with enrolment confirmed by signature on the enrolment register.
application_method: Identify and contact the prospective host department at Kyushu University (the person in charge of the exchange programme, or the faculty/graduate school student affairs office) and apply through that department; applications are not made to the International Student Center.
Confirm the application method, internal deadline and any further required documents with the host department.

Period I recruitment, around February, covers students whose studies at Kyushu University begin between April and September; Period II recruitment, around May, covers students whose studies begin between October and March.
Await the department's selection and the university's decision.
official.application_route: Apply through your prospective host department at Kyushu University during Period I (around February, for April-September starts) or Period II (around May, for October-March starts); the International Student Center does not accept direct applications.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must not hold Japanese nationality and must be a student at an overseas university.
official.international_eligibility: Yes; the scheme is exclusively for non-Japanese international students enrolled at an overseas university, including students from universities with no exchange agreement with Kyushu University.
official.duration: Period of stay of 3 months, 5 months (1 semester) or 11 months (2 semesters); acceptance in Japan must begin within the academic year.
official.description: The Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship is Kyushu University's own support program for privately financed international students, available to Special Auditing Students, Special Research Students and Double Degree Program Students who have few opportunities to apply for scholarships.
official.program_type: University-run scholarship for privately financed international exchange students (Kyushu University's own scheme)

not_confirmed: exact recruitment dates for Period I and Period II (published only as 'around February' and 'around May')
tuition_coverage (the central official pages publish no tuition waiver for this scholarship; any waiver comes from the specific exchange agreement or a faculty-level description)

travel_coverage (no travel benefit is published on the central official pages; the FY2018 edition of the scheme guidelines on Kyushu's own domain mentions travel expenses reimbursed up to JPY 50,000 for Asia and JPY 100,000 outside Asia)
documents (the current official pages publish no document list; the host department sets requirements)
english_requirement (no English test or MOI requirement is published for this scholarship)
verification.notes: Checked the Kyushu University Global Gateways (International Student Center) Tuition, Fees and Scholarships page in English and Japanese, Kyushu University's INVITATION site for prospective international students (which publishes 支給額 月額80,000円), the Kyushu University Financial Aid page, and the FY2018 edition of the Friendship Scholarship scheme guidelines on isc.kyushu-u.ac.jp. The JPY 80,000 monthly amount, the eight published main requirements and the two recruitment periods come from those pages. The URL in the assignment (kyushu-u.ac.jp/en/admissions/financial-support/scholarships/international) returns 404, so the current official pages are cited instead; the FY2018 guidelines are cited only as a clearly dated secondary source and their document list and travel caps are not recorded as current.

applicant_utility.summary: Kyushu University's Friendship Scholarship pays JPY 80,000 a month to non-Japanese students from overseas universities who come to Kyushu U as special auditing, special research or double-degree students and cannot fund the stay themselves. There is no central application: your prospective host department runs the application during one of two annual recruitment rounds, around February for April-September starts and around May for October-March starts. The published central rules cap your combined scholarship income at JPY 80,000 a month, so this award generally cannot be stacked with JASSO for the same months, and it is living-cost support only, not tuition funding. Kyushu U publishes more than one description of a scholarship with this name on its own sites, so get your host department to confirm in writing which terms apply to you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Japanese students at overseas universities, with or without an exchange agreement with Kyushu U, heading to Kyushu for a 3, 5 or 11-month special auditing, special research or double-degree stay, with strong grades (coefficient 2.30 or higher) and genuine financial need.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your prospective Kyushu U host department months ahead of the round; the department, not the International Student Center, runs the application
Confirm in writing which description of the Friendship Scholarship applies in your department (monthly amount, stay length, any fee waiver) before relying on it
Verify your stay is 3, 5 or 11 months and starts within the Japanese academic year
Obtain written confirmation from your home university that you will return to complete your degree or graduate
Check your previous-year grade evaluation coefficient (JASSO calculation method) is at least 2.30 on the 3-point scale
Declare any other scholarships you hold; the combined monthly total may not exceed JPY 80,000
Run the separate Kyushu University exchange or short-term admission procedure in parallel; the scholarship application does not cover it
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to the International Student Center instead of through the prospective host department
A previous-year grade evaluation coefficient below 2.30
A stay shorter than 3 months, longer than 11 months, or beginning outside the academic year
Holding another scholarship that pushes the combined monthly total over JPY 80,000
Being on track to complete a regular course of study at Kyushu U rather than returning to the home university, or being scheduled to withdraw or be expelled
Missing the department's internal cut-off while waiting for the university's announced recruitment window to open
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International flights to and from Fukuoka, Kyushu University tuition, examination and matriculation fees unless waived under your exchange agreement, housing deposits and initial setup, and national health insurance enrolment; none of these are covered by the central published rules. The FY2018 guidelines also warn that payment can take more than a month after arrival, so you need to land with enough cash for the first weeks.
document_audit: The university publishes no central document list, so ask your host department for the exact checklist in writing and request English wording if you need it

The FY2018 edition of the scheme guidelines still on Kyushu's own domain asks for an application form (Form 1), a transcript for the most recent year (a copy is acceptable) and a one-page A4 recommendation from the Kyushu professor who will supervise you; treat this as a guide only and confirm the current set
Expect to evidence the financial-hardship claim, your eligibility for Student status of residence, your home-university enrolment and your return commitment
Home-university transcripts and certificates may need Japanese or English preparation depending on what the department requires
Keep the Kyushu U acceptance or exchange-eligibility letter together with your home university's return confirmation, as the two are checked against each other
alerts: Kyushu University publishes more than one description of a scholarship with this name across its sites; do not rely on any faculty-level amount, stay length, travel grant or fee-waiver wording until your host department confirms it applies to you
The combined-scholarship cap means this award usually cannot run alongside JASSO for the same months, which matters if you were counting on both
No exact dates are published for either recruitment round and departments set their own internal deadlines, so a late approach can miss a round entirely
Students who finish a regular course of study at Kyushu U, or who are scheduled to withdraw or be expelled, are excluded; the award is meant for students who return home

An older edition of the scheme guidelines on Kyushu's own site mentions travel reimbursements up to JPY 50,000 (Asia) and JPY 100,000 (outside Asia), but the current pages do not mention travel support, so do not budget for it without written confirmation
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You never submit centrally: your prospective host department collects and submits the application during Period I (around February) or Period II (around May), and the university then decides.
